findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, and no ACL is set (defaults to private, but combined with no encryption this is a data protection gap for a 'reports' bucket).
The bucket stores financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding model artifacts, so data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook data is stored unencrypted at rest.

The uploaded object does not specify server_side_encryption or kms_key_id, and it is placed into reports_archive which itself lacks default encryption, so the vendor roster file is stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: unsafe force_destroy with no ACL control
findings.description: force_destroy is enabled and no ACL is explicitly set on a bucket used to hold reports, increasing risk of accidental irreversible data loss and relying on implicit defaults for access control.
